newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MAS says taking steps to improve services.
newsitem.headline: MAS says taking steps to improve services.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said on Monday it has identified key areas of service where immediate action can be taken to improve its services.
The areas included manpower and punctuality in flight departures, a MAS statement said.
The national carrier was responding to newspaper reports that shortage of pilots and cabin crew members was affecting its service.
Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sunday the government has initiated an inquiry into MAS after the reports.
Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik also said his ministry would meet with MAS officials to find solutions.
MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli said in the statement that some of the issues raised were not new. Management was aware of them and were just as concerned.

"Steps have been taken to address some of our immediate problems and long term challenges. We are constantly scrutinising our products and standards of service in areas such as catering, ground handling, inflight services and aircraft serviceability," he said.
Tajudin said MAS reviews its manpower requirements based on its planned operations.
"We are fully aware of the need for more pilots as we add to our fleet to fly to more destinations. We are now in the process of recruiting additional captains for our 737 and 747 aircraft," he said.
On its cabin crew, Tajudin said the airline has 400 new recruits currently undergoing training. "They will graduate by March this year and will be ready to serve the airline then."
MAS said some delays in departures were unavoidable due to weather and air traffic congestion, but in the case of avoidable delays, it has set a target of zero delays.
MAS stock closed up 10 cents to 6.20 ringgit on Monday.
